manifest: MOXIR rig fixtures — identity, datasheet numbers, photometry and the 3D model of each, with a source for every number
howToRead: Every spec is { value, src, basis }. `src` names an entry in `sources`. `basis` is EXACT (the maker's own page for this very model code), COMPONENT (exact data of the part inside, e.g. the lamp, when the unit's own figure is not published — conditional on that part being the one fitted), EQUIVALENT (a named fixture of the same class, because the maker publishes nothing for this field or the code could not be traced), TESTED (run on the rental units themselves — source SEVAN: the Sevan festival rig, 2026), UNKNOWN (looked for and not found: value null, said so), or ASSUMED (no source; a stated guess). Nothing here was measured by us (owner 2026-10-09: no measuring kit; the best published numbers, labelled).

identification.maker: UPlight Stage Equipment (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd. — own site pro-uplight.com, store up-light.en.made-in-china.com
identification.confirmed: UP-B380F, UP-250BSW, UP-HK1915, UP-PL5403: the model code is printed as 'Model' / 'Model NO.' on the maker's page (sources A, A2, B, B2, C, C2, C3, D). 2026-09-29: the maker's Chinese site uplight.com.cn (same company, same contact) prints model fields for UP-LA40WF too, and gives each MOXIR type's mode list (B380F 16; PL5403 8; 250BSW 24/30; HK1915 21/35/78/92/97) — still no channel ORDER for any (sources A-CN … LA-CN).
identification.notFound: UP-Q108S, UP-YH600F, UP-YZ31P: not UPlight products — absent from all 420 listings of the maker's made-in-china store, the 73 products in the pro-uplight.com sitemap, and web searches for each code. The letters read as pinyin (YZ yanwu = smoke, YH yanhua = firework, Q qizhu = gas column): probably the rental house's own labels. The real maker/model is OWED from the rental house; until then each is modelled on a named equivalent.
identification.photos: Maker photos were used to shape the models (compared by eye); they are the makers' copyright and are NOT stored in this repository.

search.gdtf: GDTF Share (gdtf-share.com), the DIN SPEC 15800 fixture library: downloading needs an account (its public API answers {"result":false,"error":"Unauthorized."}; https://www.gdtf.eu/gdtf/share_api/share-api/ : 'A GDTF Share account is required'), and its terms (https://gdtf-share.com/landing/pages/termsAndConditions.php §9) forbid commercial use and derivative works without a licence. Whether UPlight or the equivalents are listed could not be checked without logging in — the login is the owner's hand. No GDTF geometry is used.
search.openFixtureLibrary: Open Fixture Library (MIT, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLightingProject/open-fixture-library/master/LICENSE, checked at commit 4992b86, 2026-09-26): no UPlight fixtures; used only as a source of physical dimensions for named equivalents (below). OFL has no 3D geometry.
search.blenderDmx: BlenderDMX (GPL-3.0, https://blenderdmx.eu/docs/gdtffixture/) builds a Base > Yoke(pan) > Head(tilt) chain from GDTF files — the same node structure used here, but it needs GDTF files, so it is not used.
search.decision: No licensable 3D model of any of these fixtures exists, so each is BUILT here (fixtures/build_fixtures.py, Blender, headless) to the datasheet's outer dimensions and the maker's photos: Base / Yoke / Head / Lens nodes pivoting at the real pan and tilt axes.

photometryMethod: Every value is a maker's claim for an EQUIVALENT fixture (no UPlight page publishes lux or lumens: 0 occurrences across 38 store listings and every pro-uplight.com page, checked 2026-09-28). A lux figure is the centre of the beam at the stated distance and angle; candela = lux x distance^2. How the rig uses these: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs 'PHOTOMETRY' and scripts/place/README.md 'Photometry'.
